drafted_from: tool:hand-a-request-to-its-owner's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Ask an owner to run an action with what a form, a check or a person supplied, once", with {"action":{"owner":"owner-1","action_ref":"action-1"},"context":{"operation_id":"operation-1"}}. It runs tool:hand-a-request-to-its-owner and answers {"handed":["owner-action-request:operation-1:0"],"already":[],"said":"Asked owner-1: 1 request kept."}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes the owner-action-request rows already kept as records in its input, and gives back the owner-action-request rows to keep as keep.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Ask an owner to run an action with what a form, a check or a person supplied, once", and give it action; context.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:hand-a-request-to-its-owner and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: action names the owner and what is asked: owner, action_ref (or action_refs, one request each), optionally id, a fixed input, and copy rows { key, from } or { key, value } where from reads request.<field>, answers.<field> or fields.<field> of the context.

4. It reads no store and keeps nothing: give it the owner-action-request rows already kept as records (each { id, type, value }, read from your own store), so asking again is seen. Write the keep rows it returns to your own store.
